newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firmer late, interbank rate down.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firmer late, interbank rate down.

text.p: The Thai baht strengthened against the dollar in late trade on Monday as U.S. unit's weakened against the yen in overseas markets, dealers said.
The baht was traded at 26.050/26.060 to the dollar late compared with 26.060/26.110 early.
"There was dollar selling in the afternoon following its fall against the yen. As I know, there was no intervention by the Bank of Thailand," said one dealer at a local bank.
Another dealer at a European bank said some players began to sell dollars to square their position after heavily buying the U.S. unit last week.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.99 per dollar against 25.98 on Friday.
The overnight interbank rate fell sharply to 15.00-16.00 percent late from 20.00-22.00 early on easing demand for funds, dealers said.
"Banks were willing to lend funds in the market today and the demand for funds is relatively easing. The interbank rate is likely to ease further tomorrow," one money market dealer said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium edged down to 17.00/18.00 satangs per a dollar late from 19.00/20.00 early.
